_comment: REPORTING 5 and METRICS 11 vectors, written by spec/tools/report_reference.py --write and checked by running it without arguments. Signatures are deterministic (RFC 6979) so the file is reproducible; real clients may sign with random k, so apps compare by verifying, not by bytes. Header names are case-insensitive; bodies are the exact UTF-8 bytes sent.

rfc6979.comment: RFC 6979 A.2.5 (P-256, SHA-256): checks deterministic signing; apps check only verification.

verify.name: s replaced by n - s is valid too (the original is low-S; servers must accept both)
non-zero trailing bits in the last base64url character are malformed
signed the SHA-256 digest instead of the message (hashed twice)

publicKeys.name: x not below p (32 bytes, unreduced)
public key that contains the private d

server.name: per-device rate limit (policy: burst 3, then one accepted report per 4 s)
API key required; a device is bound to its account; an explicit transfer moves the username (policy: transfer allowed)
body size limit; unknown fields are ignored

scheduler.name: steady activity, then idle heartbeats, then quiet
a report that fails twice is lost; the next window starts where it ended
one retry after 2 s sends the same report
429 with Retry-After 20: usage during the wait is never reported
a tick gap over 15 s (sleep) discards the open window
pause sends a leaving report; resume starts a new window
network switched off: no leaving report, nothing sent until it is back
activity after idle sends at once, then every 5 s
consecutive failures back off (5 s after the second lost report)
pause during a Retry-After wait sends no leaving report
pause during a backoff still sends its leaving report (one attempt)

discovery.name: a minimal document gets the defaults; apiKey.mode is none
optional links that are not https are dropped; the document stays valid
optional links of a loopback test server are dropped too (links are always https)
an optional link of the wrong type makes the document invalid
terms that are not https make the document invalid
loopback http terms are invalid even from a loopback test server
a missing privacy link makes the document invalid
a loopback http api is accepted from a document fetched over loopback http
a loopback http api in a document fetched over https is invalid
an http api with any other host is invalid
an api with a query is invalid
numbers outside their ranges are clamped; the heartbeat never below the interval
unknown fields and section names are ignored (machineTraffic is no longer a section)
